items.title: Birth Is Upon Me, Death Is Upon Me
items.note: Belfast trio using the studio as an instrument, threading fiddle and guitar through heavily improvised, electronics-tinged jazz. Inspired by personal loss and their Northern Irish surroundings, it's atmospheric and genuinely moving.

items.title: Songs For Sinners
items.note: His first album in six years, mixing gospel, jazz and Caribbean soundsystem rhythms with 808s. London jazz with a dancefloor pulse, from one of its best drummers.

items.title: Nu Zamrock
items.note: Third album, reimagining 1970s Zambian Zamrock through hip-hop, poetry and soul. Confident and rhythm-forward, rooted in her own family history.

items.title: Late Loop
items.note: First album in five years, built under strict self-imposed rules, with vocals from Alison Skidmore and Elaine Howley threaded through his usual heavy, waterlogged low end. Still unmistakably his own sound.

items.title: Places Remember Events
items.note: upsammy and Piezo's debut as a duo, made across the Netherlands and Italy. Elegant, angular electronica mixing her ambient instincts with his bass and techno leanings, with a nostalgic streak running through it.

items.title: Music for Empty Stadiums
items.note: John Talabot's new ambient alias, a 17 track, 95 minute beatless record made during lockdown. Patient and uneventful in the best way, built for empty rooms rather than dancefloors.

items.title: Burning Song
items.note: Recorded alone at Leipzig's Thomaskirche, her first solo album in two years. Slow moving pipe organ drone that rewards full attention, with more weight and grief in it than usual.
Debut album, described as a rock record with no guitars: live drums and bass colliding with synths and samples, with James Murphy producing one track. Restless and narcotic, built for moving.

items.title: Begin Yr Singing
items.note: A Chicago supergroup's debut, six live-tracked instrumentals with two overdriven guitars and improvised horns. Somewhere between Sonny Sharrock and Crazy Horse, loose and physical.

items.title: Final Circle
items.note: A five track meeting of Skee Mask's dub ambience and North Americans' dreamy Americana guitar work. Understated and warm, good for the long nights coming.
